national.title: How to Apply for a New Electricity Connection in India (2026)
national.summary: Master procedure for obtaining a new low-tension domestic electricity connection from state distribution companies across India. Verified guide covering contracted load calculation, licensed electrical contractor wiring certificates, statutory security deposits, and meter installation.

steps.title: Determine Contracted Load and Supply Phase
steps.description: Calculate total household electrical load in kilowatts. Standard homes require single-phase supply up to 5 kilowatts or three-phase supply above 5 kilowatts.
steps.calloutText: Under-declaring connected load leads to statutory penalties and frequent fuse tripping once heavy appliances run.

steps.title: Obtain Electrical Contractor Wiring Test Certificate
steps.description: Hire a government-licensed electrical contractor to inspect indoor wiring. The contractor issues statutory Form A completion and earthing test reports.
steps.calloutText: Distribution companies reject wiring certificates issued by unauthorized technicians without valid state electrical licenses.

steps.title: Register on State DISCOM Consumer Portal
steps.description: Visit the official distribution company website serving your area. Create a consumer account using your verified mobile number and email ID.

steps.title: Submit Online Application and Upload Documents
steps.description: Fill the new service connection form (A-Form). Upload scanned copies of identity proof, registered ownership deed, and wiring test reports.
steps.where: State DISCOM Portal or Sub-Division Office
steps.calloutText: Ensure scanned property documents clearly show survey numbers and boundary descriptions to prevent inspection delays.

steps.title: Undergo Technical Feasibility Site Inspection
steps.description: A distribution company junior engineer visits the property to inspect premises feasibility, service line route, and earthing pit safety.
steps.calloutText: Ensure clear access to the exterior meter installation location and keep electrical test reports on site.

steps.title: Pay Statutory Quotation and Security Deposit
steps.description: After technical clearance, the utility issues an official demand notice. Pay the load security deposit and service connection charges online.
steps.calloutText: Pay the quotation demand notice within thirty days to keep your sanctioned load reservation active.

steps.title: Install Service Line and Smart Energy Meter
steps.description: Utility linesmen draw the service wire from the nearest distribution pole. They mount the tamper-proof electronic smart meter on the outer board.
steps.calloutText: Meters must be mounted on accessible outer walls at eye level to allow regular monthly reading and maintenance.

steps.title: Energise Power Supply and Receive First Bill
steps.description: The distribution linesman connects the main cut-out fuse and energises supply. Save the signed meter installation report for billing records.
steps.calloutText: Your consumer account number becomes active immediately and reflects in the online portal for monthly payments.

documentRequirements.name: Applicant Identity Proof
documentRequirements.description: Valid government-issued identity card showing full legal name and photograph.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Original for verification and 1 self-attested photocopy or scanned PDF.

documentRequirements.name: Proof of Lawful Property Ownership
documentRequirements.description: Registered sale deed, gift deed, allotment letter, or recent municipal property tax paid receipt.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Self-attested photocopy and registered index copy.

documentRequirements.name: Licensed Electrical Contractor Test Report (Form A)
documentRequirements.description: Official wiring completion and earthing safety certificate signed by an authorized electrical supervisor.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Original signed and stamped certificate with supervisor licence number.

documentRequirements.name: Registered Rent Agreement and Landlord NOC
documentRequirements.description: Valid registered tenancy agreement along with signed owner no-objection certificate for electricity connection.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Original landlord NOC on non-judicial stamp paper and registered agreement copy.

documentRequirements.name: Adjacent Consumer Electricity Bill Copy
documentRequirements.description: Recent electricity bill of adjacent neighbour or same building to identify feeder line and transformer pole.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Photocopy of recent energy bill showing consumer number.

documentRequirements.name: Trade Licence or Business Registration
documentRequirements.description: Shop and Establishment licence or GST certificate for non-domestic commercial power connections.

documentRequirements.name: Co-Owner Consent and No-Objection Letter
documentRequirements.description: Affidavit or signed consent letter from other co-owners if property is jointly owned.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Notarised consent affidavit from all legal co-owners.

fees.label: Online Application Registration Fee
fees.description: Standard administrative processing fee charged upon registration of application.

fees.label: Security Deposit per Kilowatt (Single Phase)
fees.description: Statutory refundable security deposit collected per kilowatt of contracted domestic load.

fees.label: Smart Energy Meter Security and Testing Charge
fees.description: Statutory laboratory testing and meter equipment deposit for single-phase electronic meter.

fees.label: Standard Service Line Development Charge
fees.description: Fixed service connection charges covering cable drawing up to thirty meters from nearest pole.

rejectionReasons.title: Unlicensed Wireman Wiring Report
rejectionReasons.description: Submission of wiring test certificate issued by an unauthorized electrician without active state licensing.
rejectionReasons.solution: Hire a government-licensed electrical contractor registered with the state licensing board for inspection.

rejectionReasons.title: Outstanding Dues on Premise
rejectionReasons.description: Pending unpaid electricity bills on the same premises from a previous tenant or owner.
rejectionReasons.solution: Clear outstanding dues with the utility or submit proof of fresh purchase clearance indemnity bond.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Landlord No-Objection Certificate
rejectionReasons.description: Tenants applying without formal written consent from the registered property owner.
rejectionReasons.solution: Submit an original notarised NOC signed by the property owner along with recent ownership proof.

rejectionReasons.title: Inaccessible Outdoor Meter Placement
rejectionReasons.description: Installing the meter cabin inside locked private areas or hazardous damp spaces.
rejectionReasons.solution: Relocate the meter board to an accessible outer ground-floor wall away from rain and hazards.

rejectionReasons.title: Transformer Feeder Overload
rejectionReasons.description: The local distribution transformer lacks surplus capacity to support requested electrical load.
rejectionReasons.solution: The utility plans network enhancement or requests applicant deposit work for dedicated distribution transformer.

rejectionReasons.title: Name Discrepancy on Title Deeds
rejectionReasons.description: Name on applicant identity card does not match spelling on registered property deed.
rejectionReasons.solution: Upload a notarised name discrepancy affidavit or official gazette notification confirming legal name.

faqItems.question: How many kilowatts of load do I need for a 2-BHK home?
faqItems.answer: A standard 2-BHK apartment typically requires two to four kilowatts for lights, fans, refrigerator, and one air conditioner.

faqItems.question: Can a tenant apply for an electricity connection directly?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Tenants can apply by submitting a registered rent agreement and a signed no-objection certificate from the owner.

faqItems.question: What is a wiring test report and who issues it?
faqItems.answer: It is a statutory safety document certifying indoor wiring and earthing, issued by a licensed electrical contractor.

faqItems.question: How long does a distribution company take to release power supply?
faqItems.answer: Under National Electricity Rules, distribution companies must energise supply within seven to fifteen days after fee payment.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between single phase and three phase supply?
faqItems.answer: Single phase handles loads up to 5 kilowatts. Three phase supports heavier residential loads exceeding 5 kilowatts.

faqItems.question: Why is an adjacent electricity bill requested during application?
faqItems.answer: It helps the field linesman pinpoint the exact distribution pole, transformer capacity, and sub-division route quickly.

faqItems.question: Is the electricity security deposit refundable?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The security deposit remains refundable and earns interest or is adjusted when closing the connection permanently.

faqItems.question: What should I do if the previous occupant left unpaid bills?
faqItems.answer: Submit ownership transfer proof and indemnity bond to sub-division officers to isolate past arrears from new service.

items.title: Calculate Connected Appliance Wattage
items.description: Sum up wattages of lights, geysers, and air conditioners to request accurate contracted load.

items.title: Secure Licensed Contractor Wiring Certificate
items.description: Obtain signed Form A certificate and earthing test report from a licensed electrician.

items.title: Check Outstanding Premise Dues
items.description: Confirm the premises has no past unpaid electricity balances from previous owners.

items.title: Prepare Ground Floor Outdoor Meter Board
items.description: Mount an accessible weatherproof meter cabin on the exterior wall near property gate.

items.title: Keep Scanned Ownership Documents Ready
items.description: Have clear digital PDF copies of registered sale deed and identity proofs on hand.

GJ.title: How to Apply for New Electricity Connection in Gujarat (2026)
GJ.summary: Gujarat distribution is managed by GUVNL subsidiaries (DGVCL, MGVCL, PGVCL, UGVCL) and Torrent Power. Applications are processed online via Digital Gujarat or dedicated DISCOM portals with doorstep smart meter installation.
